chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Ahmad ibn Zakariyya al-Saydalanī from a man from Banu Hanifa, from the people of Bust and Sijistan, who said:

I accompanied Abu Ja'far al-Jawad (peace be upon him) in the year he performed Hajj in the early days of the caliphate of al-Mu'tasim. I said to him while I was with him at the dining table, and there was a group of the governors of the ruler: 'Our governor, may I be your ransom, is a man whom the Ahl al-Bayt love and who loves them, and I have a land tax (kharaj) recorded in his diwan. If you see fit, may Allah make me your ransom, that you write to him to treat me well.' He said, 'I do not know him.'

I said, 'May I be your ransom, he is as I said, one of the lovers of the Ahl al-Bayt, and your letter will benefit me with him.' So he took the paper and wrote: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As for what follows, the bearer of my letter has mentioned about you a good disposition, and whatever of your deeds you have done well, do good to your brothers, and know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will ask you about the weight of a speck of dust and a mustard seed.'

When I arrived in Sijistan, the news preceded me to al-Husayn ibn Abdillah al-Naysaburi, who was the governor. He came out to meet me from the city at a distance of two farsakhs. I handed him the letter, so he kissed it and placed it on his eyes. Then he asked me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'A land tax upon me in your diwan.' He said, so he ordered it to be removed from me and said, 'Do not pay land tax as long as I have authority.' Then he asked me about my family, and I informed him of their number. He ordered for me and for them what would feed us and a surplus. So I did not pay land tax during his tenure as long as he was alive, nor did he cut off my connection (of favor) until he died.

key_terms.الْجَوَادُ: Al-Jawad (the Generous), title of the 9th Imam
key_terms.الْفَرْسَخَانِ: Two farsakhs, a unit of distance
key_terms.دِيوَانِهِ: His diwan, administrative record or office
key_terms.مَثَاقِيلُ الذَّرِّ: Weights of dust, referring to small deeds

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Jawad (AS) use a short letter to influence a governor's administrative decisions?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical intercession (*tawassul*) of Imam al-Jawad during the Abbasid era, highlighting how the Imams leveraged their spiritual authority to secure material relief for their followers. The Imam’s concise letter, emphasizing that God holds individuals accountable even for the weight of a mustard seed, serves as a theological reminder of divine justice that effectively moved the governor to permanently exempt the narrator from land tax (*kharaj*).
